item.title: Increased Hemoglobin With SGLT2 Inhibitors
item.description: Inhibitors of the sodium-glucose transporter 2 (SGLT2i) were developed to improve metabolic control of diabetes by inducing urinary glucose excretion. When tested for cardiovascular safety, use of SGLT2i surprisingly showed improvements in cardiovascular and kidney outcomes. SGLT2 inhibitors have now become firmly established as guideline-recommended therapy in patients with diabetes and high cardiovascular risk, in patients with heart failure, and in those with chronic kidney disease (CKD).

item.title: SGLT2 Inhibitor Use and Levels of Hemoglobin, Markers of Iron, and Erythropoiesis
item.description: This meta-analysis of clinical trials of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors examines the association of SGLT2 use with increases in levels of hemoglobin and hematocrit.

item.title: JAMA Editors' Summary Podcast October 23, 2026
item.description: Listen to the JAMA Editor’s Summary for an overview and discussion of the important articles appearing in JAMA.

item.title: New Guidelines Issued for Diagnosing Iron Deficiency
item.description: The American Society of Hematology (ASH) released updated guidelines for diagnosing iron deficiency, aiming to reduce missed diagnoses by standardizing ferritin thresholds across patient populations.

item.title: WHO Reports Highest Number of Cholera Deaths in Decades
item.description: The World Health Organization (WHO) found that deaths from cholera increased in 2025, despite a lower number of reported cases. The WHO also provided updated data on bacterial meningitis in Africa in 2025 as well as human plague.

item.title: Global Heart Failure Burden Increased Between 1990 and 2023
item.description: The global burden of heart failure increased sharply from 1990 to 2023, reaching an estimated 56 million cases worldwide, according to a cross-sectional study published in JAMA Cardiology.

item.title: ACC Releases Guidance for Managing Resistant Hypertension
item.description: The American College of Cardiology (ACC) released new guidance on blood pressure management for patients with resistant hypertension.

item.title: AAP Advises Against Raw Milk and Other Unpasteurized Dairy
item.description: The American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) released an updated policy statement outlining the risks of unpasteurized dairy consumption.

item.title: WHO Publishes First Guidelines for Managing Obesity in Children
item.description: The World Health Organization (WHO) published its first guidelines on the management of obesity in children and adolescents.

item.title: Steatotic Liver Disease: A Global Problem
item.description: This Medical News article discusses international efforts to determine the prevalence and increase awareness and detection of steatotic liver disease, which affects an estimated 1.7 billion people worldwide, including most individuals with obesity or type 2 diabetes.

item.title: The Rise in Testosterone Therapy for Women
item.description: This Medical News article discusses growing use of testosterone therapy among women, and a US Food and Drug Administration public workshop that explored the current evidence on its use beyond sexual function.

item.title: Trastuzumab Rezetecan in EBBR2-Low Metastatic Breast Cancer
item.description: Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) combine the tumor-targeting specificity of a monoclonal antibody with a cytotoxic payload, using a chemical linker designed to remain stable in the bloodstream and to release the drug selectively within tumor cells. Third-generation ADCs can exert a bystander effect, whereby the payload diffuses into neighboring tumor cells, killing them independently of target expression. The drug to antibody ratio further modulates potency and tolerability. ADCs have transformed the life expectancy of patients with erythroblastic oncogene B (ERBB2; formerly HER2/neu)–overexpressing breast cancer and are rapidly expanding into new tumor types and molecular subgroups.

item.title: Trastuzumab Rezetecan in ERBB2-Low Advanced Breast Cancer
item.description: This randomized, multicenter, phase 3 trial compares progression-free survival with trastuzumab rezetecan vs physician’s choice of chemotherapy in patients with ERBB2-low metastatic breast cancer.

item.title: Trastuzumab Rezetecan in ERBB2-Low Advanced Breast Cancer Research Summary
item.description: This trial compared trastuzumab rezetecan vs physician’s choice of chemotherapy in patients with erythroblastic oncogene B (ERBB2)–low metastatic breast cancer.
